tasks.short: Apply 3D or time-aware 4D GIS methods to support new analyses.

steps.what: Choose a three-dimensional or time-aware analysis appropriate to the spatial question
Prepare elevation, geometry and time fields for the chosen GIS representation
Build the 3D scene or temporal model and configure the analysis
Check elevation alignment, temporal interpretation and whether the analysis answers the question
Save the approved model and analysis settings in the internal GIS workspace

tasks.design: Configure dimensional-data preparation recipes and scene templates in the GIS tooling category of {OTHER}. Reuse validated elevation and time mappings, layer styling and model setup while retaining the choice of analysis and complete spatial-temporal checks; save the accepted model only after final review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Elevation datums, time conventions and scene setup vary between sources and projects.
tasks.enabler_now: Native GIS processing recipes and reusable scenes can remove repeated configuration for comparable data.
tasks.still_hard: A visually convincing model can have the wrong vertical datum or imply movement between unrelated observations.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an analysis justified by the spatial and temporal resolution and explain its limits.

ambition.what: Provide a time-aware site-development comparison showing approved elevation changes between survey dates.

tasks.altitude: Spend less time rebuilding scene settings and more time assessing what the model establishes. Analysis acceptance rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Observation identity, temporal validity and coordinate reference governance

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: GIS tools can reuse elevation mappings, temporal settings and scene templates. The proposed application and savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary includes selecting, preparing, constructing, reviewing and saving a 3D or 4D analysis. Survey acquisition and external publication are separate tasks.

Dataset producers supply feature ID, geometry, horizontal reference system, vertical datum, elevation unit, observation timestamp, timezone and acquisition method. s1 chooses the valid analysis and s2 checks mappings; missing datum or time meaning requires manual clarification, never guessed conversion.

s2 and s3 retain manual setup for novel inputs and analysis-specific choices. Savings apply only to repeated human field mapping, styling and scene configuration, not GIS computation already performed automatically.
The native {OTHER} recipe and scene configuration is tested before custom code. s4 checks datum alignment, temporal continuity, uncertainty and question fit, not just successful rendering.
s5 stores the final scene, source revisions and settings only after s4 approval. Estimates need observed task timings and compatible-source coverage.
unknowns: Source datum and time metadata quality
research_questions: Do reused settings preserve vertical accuracy and avoid misleading temporal interpolation?

already_counted.description: Check spatial-temporal meaning and final analysis suitability

incremental.description: Maintain dimensional mappings, scene templates and validation examples

approvals.approved_version: Final 3D or 4D model revision, source dataset versions, transformations and workspace approved in s4; any change requires another review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 20.5% removes 10 preparation, 7.5 repeated scene-setup and 5 saving hours, less 2 upkeep. Low assumes every project needs new dimensional mappings and scene configuration, leaving only the controlled save return. Analytical choice and final meaning checks keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Apply reusable GIS setup while retaining responsibility for spatial and temporal validity.
reach: Data warehousing specialist temporal observation modeling
role.ambitious_version: Offer verified survey-date comparisons with explicit limits on vertical accuracy and temporal interpretation.

job.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
